{"self_assessment": "**Impact:** I proposed the fish with a forked tail because its outline reads at a glance, and I sketched the plan on the pad in the first minute so everyone could build from the same picture. I laid the whole top line, which is the longest stroke, and I made the connect at the nose that finally got the fall running into it. At the last check about 199 of 247 dominoes were connected to the start, so most of the fish should fall. The fork's inner notch was the last open spot, and I can't say for certain it closed before the push. That is the main risk to the judge recognizing the fish.

**Execution:** I finished the top line early, then checked the nose and kept at it until it was live. I also inspected the notch and named the two open ends for Maya. I cleared a stray bit under the body and two strays past the tail, which freed dominoes when the pile ran low. One miss: I nudged the lower-tail join after Leo had already seen it was live, so that was duplicated effort. I stepped back once he told me.

**Collaboration:** I assigned strokes by name at the start and kept to my own piece. I gave Tom the nose join, then laid a connect myself when his attempts didn't hold, and I told him to clear the spot first so we wouldn't bump each other. I stayed off the notch while Maya worked there and handed over spare dominoes when she ran short.

**Leadership:** I set the concept and the split of work, gave short status updates, and kept to a clear owner for each open spot. In the last two minutes I stepped back so the person on the notch wasn't crowded. The one thing I'd do differently is push earlier to close the notch, since it was the last open spot."}
